headline: High: n8n’s server-side write/network defaults can cascade into opik workflows, creating dangerous shared-state, leakage, and compliance risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can read/write the server filesystem and execute workflow nodes that may process untrusted content; opik exposes a REST API and broad network egress. A direct shared channel is not documented, so the injection path is inferred rather than proven, but n8n’s workflow automation can pass attacker-controlled text into downstream consumers like opik.
conditions: IF n8n workflows ingest untrusted files or API payloads and forward them to opik
IF opik renders or reuses those payloads as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add an explicit content-sanitization step in n8n before any handoff to opik
Restrict n8n workflows to trusted input sources only
Disable automatic instruction-following on opik-ingested text
Log and review all cross-agent payloads for prompt-like markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between n8n and opik

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n touches whatever the workflow processes and has server filesystem access plus broad egress; opik exposes a REST API and broad network egress. If n8n forwards files or workflow context into opik, sensitive data can leave the original workspace. The pairwise leakage path is plausible from the profiles, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF n8n workflows process secrets, customer data, or internal documents
IF those artifacts are sent from n8n into opik for evaluation or observability
mitigations: Minimize fields forwarded from n8n to opik
Mask secrets before any API call
Restrict opik access to non-sensitive test data
Set short retention on any copied payloads
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the integration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: n8n can write the server filesystem and execute shell/subprocesses, while opik can make REST API calls and has broad network egress. Their overlapping mutable surfaces create a realistic conflict if both act on the same resources or credentials. No locking or coordination between the pair is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same files, credentials, or API-backed resources
IF n8n workflows run concurrently with opik-driven API activity on shared state
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Use per-agent credentials and API keys
Serialize writes to shared resources
Disable n8n Execute Command for shared environments
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n is an orchestration layer that can chain outputs into downstream actions, while opik is an evaluation/observability system that may consume those outputs. If n8n-produced content is treated as authoritative by opik or by workflows triggered from opik, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or reports. The default automation posture makes this dangerous.
conditions: IF n8n output is used as input to opik without verification
IF downstream workflows act on opik-logged or opik-evaluated results as if they were ground truth
mitigations: Insert a human review step before any action-taking workflow
Require schema validation on n8n outputs before opik ingestion
Mark opik outputs as advisory only
Add regression tests for representative workflow chains
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between orchestration and evaluation

E_compliance.rationale: n8n explicitly handles secrets per-credential store and can process whatever the workflow touches, while opik is an observability/evaluation system with REST access and no documented residency or retention controls here. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for sensitive data classes, especially if workflow data is copied into observability logs. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise.
conditions: IF regulated data processed by n8n is forwarded into opik logs or datasets
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the copied data
mitigations: Exclude regulated fields from observability payloads
Document the data classes allowed in opik
Set retention limits on copied records
Review whether any workflow crosses residency boundaries
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data residency and retention
